name: Prime Foods, LLC
old_description: Founded in 1936 by the Kramer family, Prime Foods produces hard-boiled eggs and on-the-go snacking solutions in southern Indiana. Prime Foods also shares its expertise through private label and contract manufacturing services.
about:
Prime Foods, LLC operates from Boonville, Indiana, where the company was founded in 1936 by the Kramer family. Now in its third generation of family ownership, the business began as a food production venture in southern Indiana and has expanded over eight decades.

The company produces hard-boiled eggs and on-the-go snacking solutions at its processing plant, which is monitored by FDA and USDA inspectors. In addition to its own product lines, Prime Foods provides private label manufacturing and contract manufacturing services for other brands. The facility follows HACCP principles and holds SQF Level 9 certification, reflecting a structured approach to food safety.

Prime Foods serves retailers and foodservice providers that require rigorous food safety management systems, as well as brands seeking private label or contract manufacturing partners. Its customer base spans the food manufacturing, snack food, and broader foodservice sectors across the United States.

The company emphasizes its multi-generational family experience and a commitment to minimizing environmental impact. It cites its SQF Level 9 certification, HACCP-based programs, and ongoing employee training as factors that differentiate its operations.

name: Prime Manufacturing Technologies
old_description: Prime Manufacturing Technologies in Howard County, Maryland has been providing one stop manufacturing solutions for commercial and government clients since 1991.
about:
Prime Manufacturing Technologies was founded in 1991 by Luke Chow in Savage, Maryland, located in Howard County. A chemical engineer by training, Chow moved from Pennsylvania after a career at Allied Corporation to start the company, initially focusing on plastic injection molding, composites, and CNC machining with an emphasis on lean and agile processes.

The company provides end-to-end manufacturing services including plastic injection molding, metal injection molding (MIM), silicone molding, CNC milling and turning, CNC electrical discharge machining (EDM), 6-axis robotic assembly and composite casting, sub-assembly, reverse engineering, 3D printing, and RFID tagging. It handles projects from rapid prototyping through short- and long-run production, operating as a one-stop shop that integrates design, mold optimization, and production under one roof.

Prime serves commercial, industrial, and military customers across agriculture, automotive, construction, defense, technology, healthcare, and telecommunications sectors. Its client roster includes Fortune 500 organizations such as Northrop Grumman, Agilent Technologies, Ciena, Snap-On Power Tools, and the Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory, alongside government agencies.

The company differentiates itself through a blend of manual craftsmanship with robotics and automation, a lean-and-agile manufacturing philosophy, and a commitment to reducing the need for multiple suppliers by covering design through final assembly.

name: Prince Manufacturing Corporation
old_description: Section 232 Steel Derivative and the Impact on Imported Hydraulic Cylinders
about:
Prince Manufacturing Corporation traces its roots to 1941, when John Prince opened a small machine shop on Water Street in Sioux City, Iowa, under the name Prince Hydraulics. His son Richard incorporated the business in September 1950 after securing a contract for 100 single-acting hydraulic cylinders, with Arthur C. Gall and F. John Roost joining as vice president and secretary/treasurer. The company now operates from North Sioux City, South Dakota.

Today Prince manufactures hydraulic cylinders and valves across multiple production facilities, all certified to ISO 9001:2015 by Amtivo. The product line includes welded-style cylinders and a range of hydraulic valves, supported by a product configurator, 3D CAD models, parts manuals, and how-to videos. The workforce numbers approximately 107 employees.

The company's early focus on the agricultural sector and the truck-and-trailer market remains central, though its hydraulic components now serve a broader industrial base. Customers include original equipment manufacturers and aftermarket distributors seeking replacement cylinders and valves for mobile and stationary equipment.

Prince was founded to meet a specific demand for simple, reliable hydraulic cylinders, and the company emphasizes its quality management system as a differentiator, with every facility holding the same ISO 9001:2015 certification.

The firm provides residential solar photovoltaic installation, battery energy storage systems, roofing and site preparation, and financing options. It manages projects from initial savings analysis through installation, with customer testimonials citing approximately six weeks from consultation to system activation. The company states its mission is to empower homeowners to embrace clean, sustainable energy through affordable options, urgent project management, and sensible solutions. It differentiates itself with a laid-back, supportive culture that it says fosters creativity and collaboration, and emphasizes being a local neighbor building stronger communities one energy-independent home at a time.

name: Pro-Fab Sheet Metal Inc
old_description: 30+ Years of Experience Manufacturing & Custom Fabrication of Sheet Metal Duct Products
about:
Pro-Fab Sheet Metal Inc was founded in 1996 in Addison, Illinois, and has grown across two generations into a multi-plant operation. The company maintains its headquarters in Addison and operates additional manufacturing facilities in Crown Point, Indiana, and Indianapolis, Indiana.

The company specializes in custom fabrication of sheet metal duct products, including rectangular duct and fittings, pipe and fittings, low-pressure pipe and fittings, as well as complex fabrications such as sound lining and double-wall thermal ductwork. It also serves as the Midwest's top distributor for Gustafson/Linx (formerly Lindab) spiral pipe and fittings, stocking those items for same-day shipment. Pro-Fab's 100,000 square feet of state-of-the-art manufacturing space across its Illinois and Indiana plants is equipped with modern technology and staffed by a union workforce, allowing it to handle orders of any size.

Pro-Fab primarily serves the HVAC industry, where it is recognized as a preferred fabricator for commercial and industrial projects. Its customer base includes mechanical contractors and construction firms requiring high-quality ductwork and related components.

The company differentiates itself through a quality control system aimed at cost efficiency, a skilled trades team that provides rapid quotations, and a dedicated fleet of trucks that ensures on-time delivery across all states. Its status as a yellow-label union shop underscores a commitment to skilled labor and reliable production.

name: Pro-Serv Food Equipment LLC
old_description: Commercial Cooking Equipment Service in North & South Carolina
about:
Pro-Serv Food Equipment LLC is based in New Bern, North Carolina. Founded in 2018 by Jared and Maria Shepherd, the family-owned business emerged from Jared’s background in commercial kitchen equipment and Maria’s experience in the restaurant sector, combining technical expertise with operational insight.

The company provides commercial food equipment services across North Carolina and bordering South Carolina counties. Its offerings include repair, sales, installation, preventative maintenance, and refrigerated box truck rental for all brands of hot-side and cold-side equipment. CFESA-certified technicians deliver 24/7 support with same-day emergency response, operating trucks stocked as mobile warehouses.

Pro-Serv serves commercial kitchens, restaurants, and food-service operations throughout North Carolina and adjacent South Carolina counties, including major metros such as Charlotte, Raleigh, Greensboro, Winston-Salem, and Wilmington. Its clients range from independent restaurants to larger facilities requiring HVAC and refrigeration support.

The company was founded to reshape the commercial kitchen service landscape by empowering small businesses with reliable, rapid-response support. Its stated differentiators include same-day emergency service, fully stocked service trucks, CFESA-certified expertise, and a customer-first approach rooted in family values.

name: ProFab, Inc.

about:
ProFab, Inc. operates from Somerset in southeastern Kentucky. The company is led by owner and president Bart Williams, with Ellie Williams serving as office manager. While a founding year is not publicly disclosed, the business has expanded its workforce and capabilities in recent years, focusing on custom metal fabrication, 3D drafting and design, and powder coating.

The shop provides start-to-finish services from concept through manufacturing, installation, and service. Core processes include CNC machining, high-definition fiber laser cutting (4 kW, capable of 1-inch carbon steel and 3/8-inch aluminum on 5-by-10-foot sheets), powder coating in an 8-by-8-by-30-foot oven, additive manufacturing with plastics and development toward 316 stainless steel, plus sand and dry-ice blasting. Design work uses SolidWorks and Autodesk Inventor, accepting native 3D model files to accelerate production.

ProFab serves a range of industries with prototypes and functional parts, though specific sectors are not listed on its site. The company emphasizes short lead times on machining jobs and uses a pallet-changing table on the laser to minimize downtime.

Management stresses reliable, consistent workmanship and a quality-over-quantity approach, with every part personally examined by a quality-control team. The integrated offering—design, fabrication, finishing, and installation under one roof—is presented as a way to reduce cost and speed delivery.

about:
ProTronics Inc. operates from Knightdale, North Carolina. The company has over 31 years of experience in printed circuit board assembly and design, though a specific founding year is not publicly disclosed. Ownership details and founder names are not stated.

The company provides a full suite of electronics manufacturing services, including PCB design, assembly (surface mount and through-hole), testing, rework and repair, IC packaging, cable assembly, and turnkey box builds. It also offers product development, new product introduction, BOM analysis, and certification management. Quality control includes 100% inspection to IPC-A-610 Class 2 and 3 criteria, using X-ray and semi-automated optical inspection for BGA and lead-less devices. Environmental testing capabilities cover ambient functional testing and ESS with hot-cold cycling and humidity. No facility size or employee count is disclosed.

ProTronics serves commercial, military, and medical electronics sectors. Its customer base includes companies such as Honeywell, MTS, Cisco Systems, Vishay Micro-Measurements, Cadence, Schneider Electric, NetApp, and academic partners like North Carolina State University. Projects have ranged from circuit boards for golf balls to implantable medical devices.

The company highlights its quick turnaround, competitive pricing, and advanced technology as differentiators. It also notes ITAR registration and RoHS compliance for regulated work.

name: Probo Medical
old_description: We focus on providing you with low-cost diagnostic imaging sales, service, rental and repair so you can focus on what you do best: delivering compassionate, high-quality care.
about:
Probo Medical operates from Fishers, Indiana, supplying diagnostic imaging equipment and services to healthcare providers worldwide. The company does not disclose its founding year or ownership structure in public materials.

The business sells, rents, and repairs new and refurbished ultrasound, cardiology, and women's health imaging systems from manufacturers such as GE HealthCare, Philips, and Mindray. Its ISO 13485‑certified facilities run a refurbishing process that tests and retests each unit to meet or exceed original specifications, backing repairs with a 90‑day warranty. The company also fields service engineers for on‑site support and runs hands‑on training courses for platforms including the Epiq, Voluson, and LOGIQ families.

Customers span hospitals, cardiology practices, women's health clinics, imaging centers, pain‑management offices, and veterinary facilities across the United States, United Kingdom, France, and Canada. Biomedical staff and medical technicians rely on Probo for probe replacements, preventive maintenance, and full‑system rentals that keep departments running during repairs.

Probo positions itself on “compromise on cost, not on care,” aiming to give clinicians affordable access to high‑quality imaging so they can focus on patient care rather than equipment budgets. The refurbishing program was built to deliver like‑new performance at a fraction of OEM pricing, with every unit passing through the certified quality system before shipment.
